ai.title: Background process manager kills process groups
ai.summary: Updated `npm-app/src/background-process-manager.ts` to spawn child processes with `detached: true` and send `SIGTERM` to negative PIDs (`-pid`). This ensures entire process groups are terminated during cleanup or shutdown, preventing orphaned child processes from lingering after the parent exits.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts helper programs to do work in the background, it now makes sure to shut down the entire family of related programs when it's done, rather than leaving some of them running unnoticed after the main one stops. This prevents leftover helper programs from consuming resources or causing confusion. If you watched the system's process list during shutdown, you'd now see all related background activity disappear together instead of pieces lingering behind.

ai.title: SIGTERM handler kills background processes
ai.summary: SIGTERM handler in npm-app/src/cli.ts awaits killAllBackgroundProcesses() before exit. Prevents orphaned processes on termination. Affects CLI signal handling.

eli5.text: When you or the system ask the assistant's command-line tool to stop (for example, when you close the terminal or a container shuts down), it now makes sure to cleanly shut down any helper tasks it had started in the background before fully exiting. Previously, those background tasks could be left running and become unmanaged leftovers. The result is that closing or stopping the command-line tool no longer risks leaving stray tasks behind.

ai.title: Add web server log configuration and login components
ai.summary: Updated `codebuff.json` to route web server stdout and stderr to `web.log`. Added new React components `LoginCard` and `LoginClientWrapper` in `web/src/components/login/` to handle CLI auth code display and general sign-in UI. These changes improve local development logging and modularize the web login interface.

eli5.text: The web server now saves its activity logs to a file called web.log instead of only showing them on the screen, which makes it easier for developers to troubleshoot problems when working locally. The login screen for the web interface has also been split into two separate pieces: one that shows a code entered during command-line authentication and another for the general sign-in view. If you opened the web login page in a browser, it looks the same to you; these are behind-the-scenes changes for local development and logging.

ai.title: Login page refactored to server component
ai.summary: web/src/app/login/page.tsx switched from 'use client' to 'use server'. Auth code expiration check moved server-side using parseInt on expiresAt. UI components extracted to dedicated files like login-card.

eli5.text: When you go to sign in to Codebuff in your browser, the page now checks whether your login code has expired before showing the sign-in form. This check happens on the company's server instead of in your browser, so your computer doesn't have to do that work. If the code is expired, you'll see the same 'Uh-oh, spaghettio!' message, but now it also shows a reminder to restart Codebuff in your terminal. This only affects people who are signing in to Codebuff through a web browser.

eli5.text: When you run certain background tasks (like a database helper and the main web program), their text logs used to get scattered into the main project folder. Now those logs are saved into a new subfolder called "debug", and that folder is set to stay private on your computer instead of accidentally being shared with others. If you look in your project folder you will see the log files no longer appear at the top level; instead they live quietly in the debug folder. This is live for anyone running these local tasks.

ai.summary: Removed `.sort()` from the file list rendering in `web/src/app/admin/file-picker/page.tsx`. Files now display in their original order from the API response. This change affects only the internal admin dashboard.

eli5.text: Admins using the internal file picker will now see files listed in the order they were returned by the system, rather than in alphabetical order. Previously, the tool automatically sorted filenames from A to Z each time the list loaded. This change does not introduce any new features or access, it only stops that sorting step, so the most recent or server-provided order is shown as-is.

ai.title: Skip startup processes if another codebuff instance detected
ai.summary: CLI skips `startupProcesses` in `codebuff.json` when another instance is running. New `startup-process-handler.ts` checks for active processes via lock files before starting dev processes. `background-process-manager.ts` adds PID-based lock file tracking to detect orphaned processes and prevent duplicate startup.

eli5.text: When you run the tool, it now checks whether another copy is already working in the same project before it starts any background tasks. If it finds an active instance running, it skips launching those duplicate background processes, preventing conflicts and wasted resources. You would notice that the usual startup messages about launching development servers or background tasks might not appear if the tool detects a similar instance already running, since it will gracefully avoid duplicating the work.

ai.title: Fix file tab completion
ai.summary: Replaces `completer` with `filePathCompleter` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to fix file tab completion. Removes dependency on `common/project-file-tree` and `fileTree`, switching to `fs.readdirSync` and `os.homedir` for direct filesystem path resolution. Adds `isDir` helper to `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` for directory checks.

eli5.text: When you're typing commands into the tool's command-line interface and hit tab to autocomplete file paths, it now actually works instead of failing or showing the wrong suggestions. The fix swaps out the old file-completion helper (which relied on a separate file-tree module and custom logic) for a simpler approach that reads directories directly from your computer's filesystem using built-in operating-system calls, and adds a small helper to tell whether a given path is a folder. If you use the CLI and press tab to autocomplete a file or folder name, you'll now get correct, real-time suggestions based on what's actually in your project folder, without needing the program to maintain its own cached view of the file structure. This is live today for anyone running the updated command-line

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.230
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.230 in npm-app/package.json. Routine release increment.

eli5.text: Today the assistant's release number moved up to 1.0.230. If you update to this version you get the new behaviors shipped on April 23: the assistant now stops its helper programs on its own after an update instead of leaving them running, and it will no longer try to start up again if another copy of the assistant is already open. You'd notice this the next time you run the assistant after taking the update.

ai.title: Refactor background process XML output
ai.summary: Refactored getBackgroundProcessInfoString in npm-app/src/background-process-manager.ts to simplify XML structure generation. Removed nested terminal_command_result tags and conditional stdout/stderr rendering. Adjusted buildArray logic to handle optional fields directly without post-filtering.

eli5.text: When the system reports on background tasks it no longer, it hides the nested XML tags like <terminal_command_result>, so the output is flatter. If you looked at the report you would see <stdout> and <stderr> only appear when there is actual content, instead of always showing empty tags, meaning cleaner output for whatever tool reads it.

ai.title: Use snapshots for background process manager tests
ai.summary: Refactored `getBackgroundProcessInfoString` tests in `npm-app/src/utils/__tests__/background-process-manager.test.ts` to use `toMatchSnapshot()` instead of multiple `toContain` assertions. Added `background-process-manager.test.ts.snap` to store expected XML-like output formats for running, completed, and errored states. This reduces test verbosity and centralizes format expectations.

eli5.text: The team cleaned up some behind-the-scenes checks that verify how the system reports on long-running background tasks, like watching test runs or build processes. Instead of repeatedly typing out each little detail they expect to see (process ID, command, status, etc.), they now save a single example of the expected output and just compare against it. Nothing you see or do changes; this only makes future updates easier to manage and less likely to accidentally break.

ai.title: Add Gemini 2.5 Flash Thinking to Lite Mode
ai.summary: Lite mode agent routing switches from Haiku to `gemini-2.5-flash-thinking`. OpenRouter stream handler now extracts `cache_read_input_tokens` via `stream_options` and adjusts cost tracking for new Gemini variants. Shared constants register the new model IDs and provider mappings across backend and common packages.

eli5.text: When you use the app in Lite mode, the assistant now switches to Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash Thinking model instead of the previous Claude Haiku model, which may change the style and speed of responses you receive. Your Lite mode usage will now be tracked with separate cost rates for this new model, so your usage and billing may reflect updated pricing for those interactions. Additionally, when the assistant retrieves content it has seen before, the system now better tracks how much of that content was reused from cache, so you may see more accurate accounting of your usage.

ai.title: Add getOpenRouterAccountInfo function
ai.summary: Added getOpenRouterAccountInfo to backend/src/llm-apis/open-router.ts. Fetches account info from https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/auth/key using env.OPEN_ROUTER_API_KEY. Logs response data to console.

eli5.text: The assistant can now look up details about its own OpenRouter account, like how many tokens you have left, by quietly contacting OpenRouter's servers in the background. This is an internal tool that staff can use to keep an eye on account usage; everyday users of the assistant won't see any new buttons or messages because of this.

ai.title: Add tag closure instruction for Gemini Flash
ai.summary: Added prompt instruction for `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-04-17` to enforce XML tag closure. Prevents malformed tool calls like unclosed `<write_file>`. Applies in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to use the newer Gemini Flash model, it now gets an extra reminder to always close every XML-style tag it writes, like finishing a note with a matching end bracket. Without that reminder, the model sometimes left tags open (for example, an unclosed <write_file>), which produced a malformed response instead of the file or action you expected. The reminder lives inside the background instructions that steer how the assistant behaves, so any time you trigger that model directly you'll see tool calls that come back properly wrapped and complete.

ai.title: Standardize environment variable to NEXTPUBLICCBENVIRONMENT
ai.summary: Replaced inconsistent `ENVIRONMENT` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT` variables with a unified `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT` across backend, common, and npm-app. This change resolves configuration drift where different services read different environment flags, ensuring consistent behavior for logging, database selection, and build processes. Updated files include `backend/src/env.mjs`, `common/src/env.mjs`, `common/src/db/env.mjs`, and `npm-app/clean-package.js`. Developers must update their local `stack.env` files to use `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT` instead of the previous variable names.

eli5.text: Your setup file that tells the app which environment you're in (like testing vs. live) used to need two different named variables depending on which part of the system was reading it. Now it just uses one consistent name everywhere, so logging, database selection, and build steps all read the same flag instead of guessing based on mismatched labels. Developers had to rename the variable in their local config file, but after that the app behaves the same as before, just without the confusion of multiple names pointing to the same thing.
